newsitem.title: USA: US's Eizenstat to meet Euro leaders again on Cuba.
newsitem.headline: US's Eizenstat to meet Euro leaders again on Cuba.

text.p: Commerce Undersecretary Stuart Eizenstat plans another visit to European leaders later this month to try to rally international action against Cuba, an aide said on Thursday.

The idea failed to take root in earlier visits because of widespread and strong criticism of Washington's anti-Cuba Helms-Burton law. The European Union decided on Tuesday to challenge the law before the World Trade Organiation.
Eizenstat tentatively planned visits in late October to France, Italy and the Netherlands, said spokesman Jim Desler.

"He (Eizenstat) does plan on going later this month and he does plan on doing what he did on earlier trips, which was focusing on areas of mutual interest," Desler said, citing promotion of democracy in Cuba.

President Clinton has suspended the most contentious Helms-Burton provision -- authority for lawsuits against foreign firms that profit from property confiscated from U.S. citizens following the 1959 Cuban revolution. He must decide in January whether or not to again suspend the provision.
Eizenstat has visited Canada, Mexico, Belgium, Ireland, Spain, Germany and Britain to seek united action on Cuba.
